assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminators on clustered templates is a genuine game-changer: it collapsed sequencing cost by orders of magnitude and underlies genomics, clinical diagnostics and much of modern biomolecular science. The chemical core (nucleotide chemistry, surface-bound clonal amplification, fluorescence detection) is squarely chemistry and has overwhelming demonstrated consequences.
assessment.attribution: The Solexa lineage (Balasubramanian, Klenerman, and Mayer for clustering/colony amplification) gives a defensible three-person configuration. Ju (terminator chemistry), Rothberg (pyrosequencing/454) and others have competing claims, so one or more strong contributors are left out.
assessment.maturity: Technology has been in universal use for roughly two decades, so recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Who among Balasubramanian, Klenerman, Mayer, Ju and Rothberg made the decisive contributions is partly a patent and commercial story that I cannot adjudicate from the supplied text.
Whether the committee views sequencing as chemistry or as a tool belonging to physiology or medicine; I am relying on my recollection of the history, not verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling is a simple, general and robust way to form aryl amine bonds and is among the most used reactions in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. It is a clear example of an approach that is easy to apply yet transformed practice.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled catalytic reaction and its mechanistic understanding; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is an important precursor but not the general catalytic method. A clean two-person prize is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and wide industrial use; the 2010 cross-coupling prize may make some members feel the area is already honoured.
uncertainties: Whether the 2010 Heck/Negishi/Suzuki prize makes this look like a second award for the same field.
Priority and credit of Kosugi's precursor and relative roles of ligand developers are from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics made it possible to simulate the motion of atoms with forces computed from electronic structure, opening up ab initio treatment of liquids, interfaces, reactions and enzymes. It tightly connects theory to experimental observables, which I value, and its influence on condensed-phase and biomolecular simulation is lasting.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper has a clean, undisputed two-person attribution, which is ideal given the three-laureate limit. Parrinello also appears in other candidates (metadynamics, machine-learned potentials), so the committee should decide how to frame his recognition.
assessment.maturity: Nearly forty years of validation and use; very mature. Computational chemistry was recognised in 2013 and 2024, which may temper urgency.
uncertainties: Potential for a broader combined computational-simulation prize in which Parrinello's other work is credited, which would change the configuration.
My own field proximity may bias me toward theory; I try to apply the same standard as for experimental candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles enabled practical in vivo delivery of siRNA and mRNA and made the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and the first siRNA drug possible. The chemistry of ionizable lipids and self-assembly is clear and the real-world consequences are unmistakable.
assessment.attribution: Cullis's group at UBC developed the key formulation and lipid concepts, and Anderson (with Langer) contributed lipid libraries and optimization. Madden, Hope and MacLachlan have strong claims too, so the three-name limit forces hard choices and credit is contested.
assessment.maturity: Clinically proven at scale, but the 2023 Medicine prize for nucleoside modification already recognised the mRNA vaccine story, which may make the field look partly served.
uncertainties: Attribution is the weak point: several people made essential contributions and a fair three-person set is unclear.
How much of the delivery lipid story is chemistry versus pharmaceutics; stated from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand breaks by chemically engineering deaminases onto a programmable Cas scaffold. It is a new kind of molecular tool with first clinical results and wide use in research, built through a chemist's approach to protein evolution and design.
assessment.attribution: Liu led both cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli as first authors of the respective discoveries. A Liu-centred prize is likely, though the 2020 CRISPR prize and the separate prime editing candidate complicate how the committee would split Liu's work. Kondo and Nishida's deaminase-fusion work is an independent related line.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation is early; real-world impact is demonstrated but not yet fully established, so timing is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether recognition should be combined with prime editing (B030) or deferred until clinical outcomes mature.
Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with Medicine-type recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Descriptor-based computational catalysis (d-band model, scaling relations, volcano plots) turned DFT into a predictive tool for heterogeneous catalyst design, with quantitative agreement to experiment in ammonia synthesis, hydrogen evolution and oxygen electrocatalysis. It is theory that predicts and is validated, which fits my standard.
assessment.attribution: Nørskov is the clear intellectual leader; Hammer, Mavrikakis, Scheffler and Rossmeisl have contributed, and credit distribution for the d-band model is shared. A single or two-person configuration is most defensible, and I would hesitate to give three without clearer priority.
assessment.maturity: Experimental validation is substantial, though some of the predictive claims remain debated in specific systems.
uncertainties: Unresolved allocation among Nørskov, Hammer, Mavrikakis and Scheffler; Hammer is not in the supplied names.
How well descriptors generalise beyond model surfaces to real catalysts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory with the funnel concept resolved Levinthal's paradox and gave a quantitative framework for protein folding, later tied to experimental mapping of folding. It shaped how the field thinks about proteins and the broader biomolecular-theory tradition I work in.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic share the funnel framework, while Dill's contribution is hydrophobic collapse and lattice models; Bryngelson and Fersht also have claims. Credit is distributed and a prize would be hard to configure without ignoring important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are mature, but the 2024 prize on protein structure prediction and design may reduce the immediate case; the theory is more conceptual than a tool.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a game-changer with consequences or primarily a conceptual framework.
Allocation of credit among Wolynes, Onuchic, Dill, Bryngelson and Fersht.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers rapidly raised solution-processed solar cell efficiencies to over 25 percent and opened a broad materials class. The speed and scale of impact are extraordinary.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskite sensitizers, Park and Grätzel made the solid-state device, and Snaith's group drove the efficiency jump; Kanatzidis and Seok also have strong claims. Credit is crowded and contested.
assessment.maturity: Operational stability and commercial viability are still unproven, so the work looks premature for a prize built on lasting consequences.
uncertainties: Long-term stability and toxicity may limit real-world impact.
Priority among Miyasaka, Park, Grätzel and Snaith is disputed.
